output.brief: The rejections were caused by our own shipping paperwork, not by the fungicide, the growers, or Meridane's equipment. After the Tallis system went live on 3 August, the Meridane mandarin bookings carried a 7°C carriage temperature instead of our 4°C specification. The product record was copied from an avocado template and never corrected, and the go-live review signed it off. The five rejected containers were all Meridane at 7°C; the 4°C containers passed, including Coastway ones with the new fungicide. Meridane's units ran to the setpoint they were given, so a refrigeration claim would be built on a false basis. I am fairly confident in this, with the main gap being that controller data is not yet tied to every pallet. Next steps, urgently: correct PRD-MAND-01 to 4°C, and check and reset the container at sea and the one queued for 10 October. Add a check that compares reefer settings with the product specification. Stop the Lower Serra suspension and the Brindle deduction. Consider independent loggers for verification.
